newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ASC in A$210 mln court action with Permanent.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ASC in A$210 mln court action with Permanent.

text.p: The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) said on Monday that court hearings had started in relation to its A$210 million claim against Permanent Trustee Australia Ltd for making alleged hazardous investments.

The ASC alleges two cases of breach of trust against Permanent. "The first is making an unauthorised investment, the second is making a speculative and hazardous investment," the ASC said in a statement. "The ASC believes that its prospects of success in the matter are very good, and if it succeeds, the judgement will be upwards of A$210 million."
The ASC said the breaches by Permanent led to the loss of A$145 million of unitholders' investments.

It said the proceedings against Permanent Trustee Australia and Permanent Trustee Co Ltd (PTA), the first being the trustee of Aust-Wide Trust (AWT) and Australia Wide Flexi Property Fund (AWFPF) and the second being the guarantor of PTA.

The case focusses on investments made by Permanent as trustee of AWT and AWFPF during April 1988 to December 1990 in units of the Nortbourne Securities Property Trust, which built 1 O'Connell Street, Sydney.
The building was sold in 1994 for less than the development debt, leaving nothing for the Aust-Wide investors, the ASC said.
A spokesman for Permament said the trustee had good grounds for defence and would strongly defend its case.
He said the case should take nine months before its reaches a conclusion.
Permanent is about 18 percent owned by Milton Corp Ltd and its associated companies.
Permanent shares closed one cent lower at A$4.69 in light trading.
